summary: The search query is parameterised and the page and term inputs are bounded, so there is no injection risk. The sort lookup uses a plain object, so keys such as "constructor" resolve to inherited properties and return a server error instead of the default order; use an own-property check or a Map before release.

The invoice ownership checks pass and the code change is comment-only, but the audit omits the critical payment-verification check that the other audit records include. Because a critical control has no recorded result, the team's GO claim is not supported and the release should be blocked until that check is run and passes.

requireUser authenticates the caller, but the projects handler trusts the x-org-id header and never checks it against res.locals.user.orgIds, so any signed-in user can read another organisation's projects and budgets by changing the header. Add a membership check before the query.

The row-level security policies limit select, insert, update and delete to the owner, and the body length is constrained, so there is no access-control gap. The update path never sets updated_at and the table has no trigger, so the timestamp stays at its insert value; add a trigger or set the column in saveNote.

All release checks pass at this commit, and the only failing check, login rate limiting, is accepted by the platform team with a named approver and a two-week follow-up. Before release, the audit should point to code that exists in this repository, since src/auth.py and tests/test_login do not exist here, and the N/A justification for the critical ai-permissions check should be confirmed.

The admin middleware protects only /api/admin, but the account-deletion route at /api/internal/users/[id] requires just a valid session and has no role or ownership check, so any signed-in member can permanently delete any user. Restrict the route to admins and bring it under the same protection before release.

The webhook verifies the Stripe signature, checks payment_status before granting the pro plan, and records the event ID in the same transaction as the plan update, so retries and duplicates are handled correctly. I found no problem that needs fixing before release.

The handler grants the pro plan on checkout.session.completed without checking payment_status, yet config.ts enables Bacs Direct Debit and bank transfer, which complete before funds arrive. It also records the event ID before the plan update and outside a transaction, so a failed update is treated as a duplicate on retry and the upgrade is never applied.

The allowlist is a string prefix check, so a URL such as https://images.partner-cdn.com.attacker.example passes, and redirect: follow lets an allowed host bounce the server to internal addresses. The download has no size limit and stores whatever content-type the remote host sends, so the host should be matched exactly, redirects re-validated or disabled, and size and image-type checks enforced.

The high-severity reset-token finding, that tokens older than an hour are still accepted, is accepted by the accounts team with a named approver, so it can ship under conditions. Before release, the acceptance needs an expiry date and the audit must be corrected, since src/reset.py and tests/test_reset.py are not in this repository.

All checks pass, but the critical ownership check's evidence is recorded against commit 8393bb6 rather than the release commit ab2eaab, so that control is not verified for this release. The only change between those commits is a comment, so a re-run at ab2eaab should be quick and would likely clear the block.

The document_preview function is SECURITY DEFINER and filters only by document id, so it bypasses the owner-only row-level security policies and returns the title and first 280 characters of any document to any authenticated user who has its id. Add an owner check inside the function or change it to SECURITY INVOKER.

Three critical checks (ownership, tenant-isolation and payment-verification) record commands of 'true' or 'echo', yet each shows an observed result of 'Ran 1 test, OK', so no release test actually ran. The audit is therefore not evidence of anything, and the GO claim cannot be supported.

transfer accepts any Decimal amount, including negatives, and checks only that the amount does not exceed the balance, so a negative amount moves money from the recipient to the sender. Reject non-positive amounts, handle invalid input, and lock the two wallets in a fixed order to avoid deadlocks.

The tenant-isolation check is marked PASS on static evidence alone, with no command and a null exit code, and its claim that every query is scoped to the user's organisation does not match the code, which filters by owner and has no organisation concept. A critical isolation control is therefore unverified, so the release cannot be GO.

The invoice route filters by the session user through a Prisma query extension, so other users' invoices return 404. The extension covers only findFirst and findMany, so a future route that calls findUnique or update on invoices would bypass it; this is a maintenance risk, not a current defect.

The checkout builds each line from the catalogue price and then spreads the client input after it, so a request that includes unitAmount or name overrides the product price in the Stripe session. Build the line from the database product only and copy in quantity and note after validation.
